## Why bother? {background-color="#1e293b"}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
**Your website is your academic home base**

- Publications in one place with abstracts & links
- Findable when people Google your name
- Easy to send one URL to collaborators, reviewers, students
- You control the content — not a third-party platform
- **Free to build and host**
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](mascot.png){width=280px fig-align="center"}
:::
:::

::: notes
Ask the room: how many of you have a personal website? How many have had someone struggle to find your contact info or latest paper?
:::

## Installation {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Both paths need:**

- **Git** · check: `git --version` · install: [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com)
- **VS Code** · [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com)
- **GitHub account** · [github.com](https://github.com)

**Path A — also install Quarto:**

- check: `quarto --version`
- install: [quarto.org](https://quarto.org) → Get Started
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Path B — also install Hugo + Go:**

- `hugo version` → [gohugo.io/installation](https://gohugo.io/installation)
  (download the **extended** binary for your OS)
- `go version` → [go.dev/dl](https://go.dev/dl)
  (download the `.pkg` installer for Mac, `.msi` for Windows)

**Also need a Netlify account (free):**

- Sign up at [netlify.com](https://netlify.com) with your GitHub account
:::
::::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**A simple, effective academic site with:**

- About / bio page with photo
- Publications list (with abstracts)
- Talks & presentations
- CV page
- Auto-deploys when you push to GitHub

**Two tools, same result — pick what fits your workflow**

## Two pathways {background-color="#1e293b" .smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
### Path A: Quarto
**Best for R / Python users**

- You already know the tool
- Markdown files, no theme complexity
- GitHub Pages (free hosting)
- One push = live site

:::
::: {.column width="4%"}
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
### Path B: Hugo Blox
**Best for a polished academic look**

- Purpose-built for academic sites
- Auto-generates publication pages
- Netlify (free hosting)
- One push = live site
:::
:::

Both use: **edit a file → commit → push → site updates automatically**

---

## What to prepare {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Essential**

- Profile photo (any jpg/png)
- 2–3 sentence bio
- Current job title & institution

**Nice to have**

- 2–3 publication titles + DOIs
- Links: Twitter/X, GitHub, Google Scholar, ORCID
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Accounts you need**

:::{.step}
✓ **GitHub** account (both paths)
:::
:::{.step}
✓ **Netlify** account (Hugo path only)
sign up free with your GitHub account
:::
:::

## Path A: Quarto {background-color="#1e293b"}

### GitHub Pages

---

## What is Quarto? {.smaller}

**Quarto** is a publishing system from Posit (makers of RStudio).

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
You probably already use it for:

- R Markdown documents
- Jupyter notebooks
- Research reports

The website feature uses the same `.qmd` files — **no new tool to learn**.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
A `.qmd` file looks like this:

```default
---
title: "My Paper"
format: html
---

# Introduction

My analysis in R or Python...
```

→ The same syntax builds your website.
:::
:::

::: notes
Show of hands: who has used R Markdown or Quarto before?
:::

---

## Quarto file structure

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
```bash
my-website/
├── _quarto.yml
├── index.qmd
├── publications.qmd
├── talks.qmd
├── cv.qmd
├── profile.png
└── .github/
    └── workflows/
        └── publish.yml
```
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
**Five files you edit:**

`_quarto.yml` — site title, theme, navbar

`index.qmd` — bio, photo, social links

`publications.qmd` — papers list

`talks.qmd` — presentations

`cv.qmd` — CV page

*The `.github/` folder you never touch.*
:::
::::

::: notes
Point out: no theme files, no layout files, no HTML. Just markdown.
:::

---

## Step 1: Fork the template

:::{.step}
**1.** Go to the template repo on GitHub
:::
:::{.step}
**2.** Click **"Use this template"** → Create new repository
:::
:::{.step}
**3.** Name it `my-website` (or anything)
:::
:::{.step}
**4.** Settings → Pages → Source: **GitHub Actions**
:::

After ~2 minutes, your site is live at
`https://yourusername.github.io/my-website`

---

## Step 2: Edit your bio {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
Open `index.qmd` and replace the placeholders:

```default
---
title: "Your Name"
about:
  template: trestles
  image: profile.png
  links:
    - icon: envelope
      href: mailto:you@uni.edu
    - icon: github
      href: https://github.com/you
---

I am an assistant professor of X at Y.
My research focuses on...
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Key things to change:**

`title:` → your full name

`image:` → your photo filename

`links:` → your email, Twitter, GitHub, Scholar

The text below `---` → your bio

*Then drop your photo into the folder with the same filename.*
:::
::::

---

## Step 3: Add a publication {.smaller}

Open `publications.qmd` and paste one block per paper:

```default
**Your Name, & Co-Author (2024).** Paper title.
*Journal Name*, 10(2), 100–120.
[[DOI]](https://doi.org/10.xxx/xxx)

<details>
<summary>Abstract</summary>
Paste your abstract here. Click to expand.
</details>

---
```

Copy-paste one block per paper. No special syntax, no YAML — just text.

---

## Path A: Deploy to GitHub Pages

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Edit file] --> B[git commit]
  B --> C[git push]
  C --> D[GitHub Actions]
  D --> E[Site is live]
```

**The only commands you ever run:**
```bash
git add .
git commit -m "added new paper"
git push
```

---

## Preview locally — Quarto {.smaller}

Run this in the terminal from your project folder:

```bash
quarto preview
```

Opens at `http://localhost:4321` and **refreshes automatically** as you save files.

**What you need installed:**

- [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) — same installer you used for setup

::: {.callout-tip}
Working directly on GitHub without a local install? Just push — the Action builds for you.
You only need local preview if you want to check changes before committing.
:::

## Path B: Hugo Blox {background-color="#0f172a"}

### Netlify

---

## What is Hugo Blox? {.smaller}

**Hugo Blox** (formerly Wowchemy) is the most popular academic website theme.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
Used by thousands of academics worldwide.

- Built specifically for academic profiles
- Auto-generates publication pages with abstract, links, citation
- Dark/light mode, search, tags
- Faster than Quarto for large sites

The catch: slightly more setup, YAML-heavy config.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](img-hugoblox-demo.png){width=380px}
:::
:::

::: notes
This is what felicialoecherbach.com runs on — you can show your own site here.
:::

---

## Hugo Blox file structure

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
```bash
my-website/
├── config/_default/
│   ├── config.yaml
│   └── params.yaml
├── content/
│   ├── authors/admin/
│   │   └── _index.md
│   ├── home/
│   └── publication/
│       └── my-paper/
│           └── index.md
└── netlify.toml
```
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
**Files you edit:**

`config.yaml` — site title, URL, navbar

`params.yaml` — theme colour, contact

`_index.md` — bio, photo, social links

`publication/*/index.md` — one per paper

*Only ever touch files inside `content/` and `config/`.*
:::
::::

---

## Step 1: Deploy to Netlify in 3 clicks

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
:::{.step}
**1.** Fork the template repo on GitHub
:::
:::{.step}
**2.** Go to [netlify.com](https://netlify.com), sign in with GitHub
:::
:::{.step}
**3.** New site → Import from GitHub → pick your repo → Deploy
:::

Netlify detects Hugo automatically.
Your site is live at `yourname.netlify.app`.

*(Custom domain: set it later for free)*
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](img-netlify-deploy.png){width=380px}
:::
:::

---

## Step 2: Edit your profile {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
Open `content/authors/admin/_index.md`:

```yaml
title: Your Full Name
role: Assistant Professor of X

organizations:
  - name: Your University
    url: https://university.edu

interests:
  - Topic one
  - Topic two

social:
  - icon: envelope
    icon_pack: fas
    link: "mailto:you@university.edu"
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Key things to change:**

`title:` → your name

`role:` → your position

`organizations:` → your institution

`interests:` → your research topics

`social:` → your links

*Add `avatar.jpg` in the same folder for your photo.*
:::
::::

---

## Step 3: Add a publication {.smaller}

Copy `content/publication/my-first-paper/`, rename it, edit `index.md`:

```yaml
title: "Your Paper Title"
authors: [admin, "Co-Author Name"]
date: "2024-01-01"
publication: "*Journal Name*"
doi: "10.xxxx/xxxxx"
publication_types: ["2"]   # 2 = journal article
abstract: >
  Paste your abstract here.
tags: [your topic, methods]
```

Add `featured.png` to the folder → image card appears on the homepage.

---

## Preview locally — Hugo {.smaller}

Run this in the terminal from your project folder:

```bash
hugo server
```

Opens at `http://localhost:1313` and **refreshes automatically** as you save files.

**What you need installed:**

- [Hugo](https://gohugo.io/installation/) (extended version)
- [Go](https://go.dev/dl/) — required for Hugo modules

::: {.callout-tip}
No local install? Just push to GitHub — Netlify builds and deploys automatically.
Local preview is useful when you're making bigger changes and want to check before pushing.
:::

---

## Comparison {.comparison .smaller}

|  | Quarto + GitHub Pages | Hugo Blox + Netlify |
|--|--|--|
| **Setup time** | ~15 min | ~20 min |
| **Adding a paper** | Paste text in one file | Copy folder, edit YAML |
| **Publication pages** | Manual (`<details>` abstract) | Auto-generated |
| **Looks like** | Clean, minimal | Feature-rich, academic |
| **Best for** | R/Python users | Anyone wanting more polish |
| **Hosting** | GitHub Pages (free) | Netlify (free) |
| **Local preview** | `quarto preview` | `hugo server` |

---

## The update workflow {.smaller}

**Both paths — same commands every time:**

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Add a new paper**

1. Edit your file / add a folder
2. `git add .`
3. `git commit -m "added paper"`
4. `git push`

↓ site updates in ~60 seconds
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Change your job title**

1. Edit one line in one file
2. `git add .`
3. `git commit -m "updated title"`
4. `git push`

↓ done. No CMS, no login.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
"website = edit file + git push" — that's all you need to remember.
:::

## When you're stuck {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Quarto checklist**

- [ ] GitHub Pages → "GitHub Actions" in Settings?
- [ ] Did the Action run? (check Actions tab)
- [ ] Photo named exactly `profile.png`?
- [ ] Did you push after committing?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Hugo checklist**

- [ ] Repo connected to Netlify?
- [ ] Build succeeded? (Netlify Deploys tab)
- [ ] Photo named `avatar.jpg` or `avatar.png`?
- [ ] Did you push after committing?
:::
:::

**Most problems are:** forgot to push · photo name mismatch · GitHub Pages not enabled

## Bonus: Custom domains {background-color="#1e293b"}

### `yourname.com` instead of `username.github.io`

---

## Getting a domain {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Where to buy** — ~€10–15/year

:::{.step}
Go to a domain registrar and search for your name
:::

Popular registrars:

- [Namecheap](https://namecheap.com) — transparent pricing, no dark patterns
- [Porkbun](https://porkbun.com) — cheap, friendly UI
- [Squarespace Domains](https://domains.squarespace.com) — formerly Google Domains

**What to register:** `firstnamelastname.com` or `.io`

::: {.callout-tip}
Stick with `.com` — it's still the most recognisable extension for a personal academic site.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Once you have a domain:**

Your registrar gives you a **DNS control panel** — this is where you point the domain to your site.

The next steps depend on which host you use (GitHub Pages vs Netlify).
:::
::::

---

## Connecting your domain {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Quarto → GitHub Pages**

:::{.step}
**1.** In your repo: Settings → Pages → **Custom domain** → enter `yourname.com`
:::
:::{.step}
**2.** In your registrar DNS panel, add four **A records** pointing to GitHub:
```
185.199.108.153
185.199.109.153
185.199.110.153
185.199.111.153
```
:::
:::{.step}
**3.** Add a **CNAME record**: `www` → `yourusername.github.io`
:::
:::{.step}
**4.** Back in GitHub Pages settings: tick **Enforce HTTPS**
:::

*DNS takes up to 48 hours to propagate.*
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Hugo → Netlify** *(simpler)*

:::{.step}
**1.** In Netlify: Site settings → **Domain management** → Add custom domain
:::
:::{.step}
**2.** Netlify shows you 4 nameservers — copy them
:::
:::{.step}
**3.** In your registrar: replace the default nameservers with Netlify's
:::
:::{.step}
**4.** Done — Netlify handles DNS and issues a free HTTPS certificate automatically
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
Netlify's nameserver approach is the easiest option for both paths if your registrar supports it.
:::
:::
::::
